name: The Indian Evidence Act, 1872
description: The Indian Evidence Act, 1872 consolidates, defines, and amends the law of evidence in India.

sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement
sections.content: This Act may be called the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. It extends to the whole of India and applies to all judicial proceedings in or before any Court, including Courts-martial...

sections.title: [Repeal of enactments.]
sections.content: [Repeal of enactments.].––Rep. by the Repealing Act, 1938 (1 of 1938), s. 2 and Schedule.

sections.title: Interpretation-clause
sections.content: In this Act the following words and expressions are used in the following senses, unless a contrary intention appears from the context: "Court" includes all Judges and Magistrates... "Fact" means and includes anything, state of things...

sections.title: "May Presume" "Shall presume" "Conclusive proof"
sections.content: Whenever it is provided by this Act that the Court may presume a fact, it may either regard such fact as proved, unless and until it is disproved...

sections.title: Evidence may be given of facts in issue and relevant facts
sections.content: Evidence may be given in any suit or proceeding of the existence or non-existence of every fact in issue and of such other facts as are hereinafter declared to be relevant...

sections.title: Relevancy of facts forming part of same transaction
sections.content: Facts which, though not in issue, are so connected with a fact in issue as to form part of the same transaction, are relevant...

sections.title: Facts which are the occasion, cause or effect of facts in issue
sections.content: Facts which are the occasion, cause or effect, immediate or otherwise, of relevant facts, or facts in issue...
